title: Rapid onramp + commitment hooks for hosted API
body:
Objective:
- Create compact messaging + quickstart flows that push low-friction dev activation into a lightweight commitment (starter credits -> small reserved commit).
- Emphasize predictability, performance, and a dev UX that lets teams ‘graduate’ from sandbox to paid in one afternoon.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Problem: devs try a hosted API, see immediate value but churn because billing feels vague and burst costs are scary.
- Win theme: move from trial curiosity to a $X/mo predictable starter commitment by making cost transparent, onboarding time short (15–60 min) and value obvious (latency + cost per call).
- Hook: short script + sample app + a single commit offer (e.g., $49/month for 500k tokens with 30-day rollback) that reduces perceived risk and buys runway.

Target audience / buyer signals:
- Early-stage product engineers and technical PMs building prototypes to demo within 1–2 weeks.
- Platform teams doing POCs for company-wide LLM features where cost predictability matters.
- Signal events: repo forks of our quickstart, repeated API keys created from same org, >500 dev tokens used in first 7 days.

Core developer-first value props to surface (headline lines):
1) "Ship LLM features that behave the same in prod — fast, predictable, and cheap to run."
2) "One API. Same SDKs. Move from sandbox to reserved in minutes without changing code."
3) "Transparent unit economics — see per-route latency and token cost instantly in the console."

Quickstart pathways (3 patterns to test):
A. 15-minute Hello-Production:
- Goal: convert cold trial -> commit in one session.
- Steps: sign up -> paste API key into CLI quickstart -> run sample endpoint -> deploy sample UI (Netlify script) -> show cost dashboard + commit CTA.
- Microcopy: "Try your first 50k tokens free. Ready to lock in predictable throughput for $49/mo?"

B. 60-minute Integration Sprint for hackweek teams:
- Goal: show measurable business value (e.g., summarization pipeline costings) and propose a 2-week reserved experiment.
- Steps: import sample repo, wire a small dataset, run end-to-end eval, run cost simulation (Optimize suggestions), propose 'starter-reserve' with telemetry.
- Microcopy: "Reserve a small pool to keep your demo smooth — no surprises, instant scale up when you need it."

C. Platform Ramp for enterprise POC:
- Goal: platform teams can onboard 5 engineers under single org with a short-term SLA and telem.
- Steps: invite team, allocate per-route budgets, enable prefix caching, run performance smoke tests, offer 30-day pilot pricing with rollback.
- Microcopy: "Pilot with guardrails: SLA-backed pilot and a single easy invoice at month-end."

Pricing-language drafts (test variations):
1) Transparent-unit framing (developer-friendly):
- "Pay per token. See exact token price per model and latency band in the Console. Free 50k tokens to try."
- CTA: "Estimate your monthly bill with our simple calculator."

2) Starter-commit: risk-limited monthly reserve:
- "Starter Plan — $49/mo for 500k tokens. Rollback within 30 days. Priority queueing disabled. Upgrade any time."
- Rationale: low dollar anchor reduces fear; rollback reduces perceived risk; keeps price testing simple.

3) Seat-lite + compute credit (platform teams):
- "Team Starter — $150/mo + $100 compute credit, includes org-level analytics and two seats."
- Use-case: early platform adoption where visibility matters more than raw token unit pricing.

Microcopy & email snippets (developer-facing):
- Sign-up banner: "Get 50k tokens free — build in minutes, commit when you’re ready."
- In-console modal after demo run: "Loved the latency? Lock in predictable throughput for just $49/mo and keep your demo stable."
- Quick email follow-up (post-quickstart): "Hey — saw you ran the demo. Want to reserve a small pool so your app never slows during demos? 30-day rollback. Reply 'start' to get set up."

Competitive positioning notes (short bullets):
- OpenAI / Anthropic: strong brand + dev mindshare; our counter is operational predictability and one-click reserved capacity that doesn’t force self-hosting.
- Cloud vendor managed endpoints: tend to be higher friction on per-developer onboarding; we lean on simplicity (SDKs, prebuilt quickstarts) and transparent token economics.
- Self-hosted runtimes: lower unit cost at scale but high ops burden. Pitch: if you want control without hiring a cluster team, use Redwood Dedicated/Private when you’re ready — hosted API gets you productivity first.

Differentiation hooks to test in copy:
- "Same API from prototype->SLA-backed prod" (bridge the dev->prod gap)
- "Predictable bill, not surprise spikes" (pricing clarity)
- "Ship without managing GPU ops" (no infra lock-in)

A/B test matrix (first 6-week experiment):
- Variant 1 (control): existing onboarding flow + free tokens messaging.
- Variant 2: show explicit starter-reserve offer at end of quickstart modal ($49/mo).
- Variant 3: show usage-based cost-estimate dial pre-signup (interactive).
- Metrics: commit conversion rate (7d/30d), retention after commit (30d), churned trial > paid.

Metrics & instrumentation to capture:
- Quickstart completion rate (clicks on 'deploy sample UI')
- Time-to-first-successful-generate (minutes)
- Conversion-to-starter (within 24h and 7d)
- Average monthly tokens per starter plan user
- Support interactions per onboard (NPS-ish proxy)

Unresolved questions / open items (notes to self):
- How many free tokens is optimal to nudge commit without over-subsidizing? 25k vs 50k vs 100k.
- Legal: does a 30-day rollback need extra billing terms? Check with finance. (linked ticket: JIRA-GTM-789)
- UX: where to place the reserve CTA without breaking experimentation? homepage, console modal, or end-of-quickstart screen?

Sample playbook for SDRs / Developer advocates (short):
1) Run the 15-min quickstart with the prospect during a screen share.
2) Show cost dashboard, run a short latency comparison (our host vs cloud-hosted pair).
3) Offer the $49 starter reserve as an easy next-step — explain rollback.
4) If they are platform-y, push Team Starter + invite flow and show org analytics.

Notes on tone and language:
- Keep it pragmatic and low-ceremony. Engineers react to concrete numbers not marketing adjectives.
- Use 'predictable' not 'cheap' — $ anchors matter.
- Avoid 'enterprise' language in initial flow; use it when the platform signals escalate.

Next steps / owners:
- Build quick modal prototype (Design) — owner: Priya N. — due 2024-11-20.
- Implement starter-plan product SKU + billing rollback flow (Finance + Product) — owner: Omar E. — due 2024-12-05.
- Hook up experiment tracking for conversion (Analytics) — owner: Miguel S. — due 2024-11-25.

Related links & artifacts (for quick reference):
- Quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (PR #56 has sample Netlify deploy)
- Pricing epic (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-1234
- Experiment ticket: JIRA-GTM-789

Rough brainstorm snippets (untidy):
- "starter-reserve" should appear in CLI flow as --reserve=starter or --trial=50k shorthand
- Slack snippet for engineer-to-engineer invite: "Hey I tried Redwood hosted — 25k free tokens and $49/mo starter if you want stable demos"
